mechanism: Custom CorrelationMatrix indicator: over InpWindowSize (default 60) bars, build flat returns[window×K] for K symbols; column-mean center; sample covariance Cov[a,b]=Σ centered_a·centered_b/(n−1); corr=Cov/(σ_a σ_b) clipped to [−1,1]; plot average off-diagonal correlation in a separate window as a portfolio-wide coupling state.
data_needed: Synchronized closes/returns for N symbols; window size; flat returns and K×K correlation buffers; valid-observation skips for missing ticks.
why_new_for_mis: Turns a rolling multi-asset correlation matrix into a single average-coupling regime coordinate—MIS can tag low-corr diversification vs high-corr stress regimes without single-pair Pearson snapshots.
quote: Many trading systems monitor correlations between instruments to detect regime changes or to construct mean-variance efficient portfolios. The following custom indicator computes a rolling correlation matrix for multiple symbols and displays the average correlation in a separate window.

mechanism: Explicit market fact used as sensing motivation: under stress, cross-asset correlations jump toward 1, collapsing diversification and invalidating static hedges. A rising average (or eigenvalue bulk) of the rolling correlation/covariance matrix is the change event that should re-trigger hedge re-estimation.
data_needed: Rolling multi-symbol correlation or covariance matrix over time; stress vs calm baseline of average corr / largest eigenvalues.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-asset FX portfolios generally; pair example EURUSD–GBPUSD; dynamic re-estimation hourly or per tick
why_new_for_mis: Frames correlation blow-up itself as the regime-change sensor that gates when static relationships fail—MIS can fire a stress-coupling change when average corr crosses a high threshold.
quote: The financial industry has long understood that correlation is not constant. During stress periods, nearly all assets become highly correlated, undermining static hedging strategies.

mechanism: For a pair (or basket): assemble rolling ~60-day covariance of price/return series; run symmetric EVD (SMatrixEVD); take the eigenvector of the smallest eigenvalue as the cointegration / stationary combination; use that vector for instantaneous spread and hedge weights.
data_needed: Rolling covariance matrix of 2+ series; eigenvalue decomposition; min-eigenvalue eigenvector as hedge/cointegration weights.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD and GBPUSD pair-trading setup; ~60-day rolling window
why_new_for_mis: Eigen-decomposition of rolling cov yields a data-driven stationary combination sensor—MIS gets a cointegration-style spread basis that updates with the covariance regime, not a fixed hedge ratio.
quote: Compute a rolling 60-day covariance matrix of the two price series. Decompose that matrix to extract the eigenvector corresponding to the smallest eigenvalue (the cointegration vector). Use that vector to calculate the instantaneous spread and the dynamic hedge ratio.

mechanism: CAdaptiveHedge: circular buffer of last window returns for factors X and target Y; rebuild Gram XtX and Xty each update; add ridge λ·count to diagonal; Cholesky-factor and forward/back-solve (XtX+λI)w=Xty; w is the live hedge ratio(s). Re-estimates every new bar so β tracks changing linear dependence.
data_needed: Paired bar returns (or multi-factor returns); window≥3; ridge λ≥0; circular buffers; Cholesky work arrays.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: HedgeEA: chart symbol vs InpHedgeSymbol (EURUSD); InpWindowSize=60; InpLambda=0.01; new-bar OnTick; tested GBPUSD–EURUSD H1
why_new_for_mis: Online ridge-regularized β is a relationship sensor: MIS can track how one instrument’s returns load on another under numerical stability, adapting when pairwise dependence drifts.
quote: This class uses ridge regression — a regularised form of linear regression — to dynamically estimate hedge ratios between two instruments. … Add a small value λ to the diagonal of the Gram matrix (ridge regularisation) to improve numerical stability.

mechanism: Each new bar: returns r_main, r_hedge; update AdaptiveHedge → β; residual spread s=r_main−β·r_hedge; push into spread history; over last min(history,window) compute mean and sample stdev; z=(s−mean)/stdev. Enter when |z|>InpEntryZScore (2.0), exit when |z|<InpExitZScore (0.5)—scaled residual extremity as the pairs signal.
data_needed: Live β from hedge estimator; rolling residual history; mean/stdev of spread window; entry/exit z thresholds.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD main / EURUSD hedge H1; Feb–Mar 2024 backtest; entry |z|>2, exit |z|<0.5; ~1h average hold
why_new_for_mis: Z-score is on a dynamically de-hedged residual, not raw price spread—MIS gets a volatility-normalized pairs divergence sensor that stays calibrated as β moves.
quote: The EA's trading logic is based on the z-score of the spread, with entry and exit thresholds controlling trade execution. The z-score measures how many standard deviations the current spread is from its mean, providing a statistically sound basis for trading decisions.

mechanism: Volatility-targeting portfolio sketch: size each asset inverse to its own volatility, then use full covariance Σ inside a Markowitz quadratic program (min wᵀΣw subject to constraints) so allocations react to both univariate vol and pairwise cov structure—Σ must be rebuilt as markets move.
data_needed: Per-asset rolling volatilities; full rolling covariance Σ; quadratic / constrained optimiser (e.g. MinLBFGS).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-asset portfolios generally; Σ updated with market; no single TF locked in the motivation section
why_new_for_mis: Couples inverse-vol sizing with live covariance-matrix optimisation as a portfolio risk/vol sensor stack—MIS can sense when risk budgets should reshuffle because Σ or individual vols shifted.
quote: Consider a more advanced application: volatility-targeting portfolios. These strategies allocate capital inversely proportional to each asset's volatility and adjust correlations to minimise portfolio variance (Markowitz optimisation).

mechanism: PolyFitExample: last N=100 closes; build Vandermonde X with columns [1,t,t²,t³]; form normal equations XtX a = Xty; invert XtX (Gauss–Jordan with partial pivoting on flat arrays); evaluate cubic at t=N for next-bar forecast—local polynomial shape as short-horizon trend sensor.
data_needed: Last N closes on chart symbol/TF; degree-3 Vandermonde; matrix inverse of Gram; forecast scalar.
why_new_for_mis: Low-order local polynomial coefficients/forecast give MIS a shape-based trend sensor (curvature + extrapolated level) distinct from SMA/EMA slope alone.
quote: One common task in trading is estimating a polynomial trend for a given price series. … The final step is to generate a forecast for the next bar by evaluating the polynomial at t = N.

mechanism: Observation from linear-algebra gap: real financial covariance matrices become ill-conditioned when assets are highly correlated; custom inversions lose digits and near-singular failures cluster when markets couple. Conditioning / need for SVD pseudo-inverse or ridge is itself a diagnostic that the correlation regime is extreme.
data_needed: Rolling covariance of multi-asset returns; condition-number estimate or pivot/failure flags from inversion; optional SVD rank.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic 20-asset cov benchmark in article; general multi-asset FX cov from time series
why_new_for_mis: Treats numerical ill-conditioning of Σ as a market-coupling regime flag—MIS can monitor when the cov sensor itself becomes unstable because diversification collapsed.
quote: Real-world covariance matrices from financial time series are often ill-conditioned because of high correlations among assets. … A matrix that is exactly singular is rare; matrices that are "numerically singular" are common.
